Changelog

txschools 0.0.0.9000

  • Initial scaffolding.
  • TAPR public-data discovery, download, caching, and parsing.
  • Tidy/wide/raw output shapes.
  • Semantic TAPR table output via txs_get_tapr(), with legacy file-oriented TAPR access moved to txs_get_tapr_file().
  • Bulk plan and download workflow for multi-year studies.
  • Citation helpers preserving exact retrieval timestamp, source URL, and SHA-256.

Live-site rebuild (2026-07)

  • Download discovery rebuilt against TEA’s actual pages (verified live): txs_list_downloads() now parses the SAS-broker download forms and returns one row per level and dataset code, with the request method and parameters needed to execute it.
  • txs_get_tapr_file() gains a dataset argument (e.g. "REF", "STAAR1") and downloads TEA’s statewide advanced files through the broker (GET for 2024+, POST for earlier years). Broker “report page instead of data” responses are detected and raised as errors, never cached.
  • New txs_get_tapr_dictionary(): the statewide TAPR_*.xlsx workbooks are variable dictionaries, not data; they are now parsed into one tidy code/label table.
  • New txs_directory(), txs_find_campus(), txs_find_district(): name-to-identifier lookup built from TEA’s statewide reference data.
  • txs_get_src() rebuilt as a per-campus report pull (SRC has no bulk files): 2004-2012 campus reports are parsed from TEA’s fixed-width HTML into tidy masking-aware tibbles; 2013-2019 reports are cached as the official PDFs; 2020+ points to txschools.gov.
  • txs_get_aeis() rebuilt on TEA’s per-year download CGI with a dataset argument (26 datasets per level) and optional record layouts.
  • Masking hardening: values that fail numeric parsing (e.g. "< 1%") are flagged as masked with the original marker preserved; display formatting (%, $, ,) is stripped before parsing; generic TAPR page datasets keep the raw string in value alongside value_num.
  • Entity names (campus/district/county) now parse correctly from live TAPR report pages.
  • Per-source year validation (TAPR from 2013, AEIS 2004-2012, SRC 2004-2019).
  • Live smoke tests gated behind TXS_LIVE=true guard against TEA page drift.

Review fixes (2026-07, after external code review)

  • Masking fallback narrowed: only suppression-shaped markers ("< 1%", ">99%", "*", "?", "--") are flagged; year labels ("2019-20") and grade spans ("02 - 04") are ordinary text again.
  • Numeric convention standardized and documented: value_num is always the number as printed ("90%" is 90); only the semantic student datasets’ *_percent columns are proportions.
  • Generic semantic datasets gain section and row_index columns: TEA’s colspan section headings (“Grade 3 Reading”) are now context on each row instead of duplicated pseudo-records.
  • txs_get_tapr() warns (and records in the pages manifest) when a requested page cannot be retrieved, instead of returning silently empty datasets; one bad page no longer aborts a multi-page pull.
  • txs_get_tapr_file() errors on the contradictory request file_format = "html" with an explicit data_type = "advanced".
  • The getting-started vignette no longer tangles live network/cache code, so R CMD check stays offline and never touches the user cache.

Cache visibility tooling (2026-07)

  • New txs_cache_size() summarizes cache size, optionally grouped by one or more of source, year, level, data_type, dataset.
  • txs_cache_size() and txs_cache_delete() share one filter set – source/year/level/data_type/dataset/older_than (a Date, POSIXct, or a number of days) – so a size preview always matches what the same delete call would remove. Files whose sidecars lack a retrieval timestamp are never matched by older_than.
  • txs_cache_list() results now print a short summary header (file count, total size, retrieval date range when known) before the usual tibble output, and gain a dataset column.

PEIMS finance (2026-07)

  • New source: TEA’s PEIMS “single file” financial data downloads. txs_get_peims_finance(year, basis, type) pulls one statewide fund/function/object-level budget or actual file for districts or charter schools, school years 1999-2000 onward – the district actual files run to several million rows per year.
  • The data arrives already long; the tidy output types the amounts, zero-pads the code columns, and (by default) joins human-readable fund/function/object/program-intent labels plus district and campus names from TEA’s companion “multiple file” code tables, degrading gracefully to codes-only when those tables cannot be fetched. Charter files’ nonprofit chart of accounts is normalized into the same columns.
  • New txs_write_peims_db() writes results to DuckDB (one table per year/basis/type plus a _peims_meta provenance table), and the getter’s db argument writes through directly, so multi-year databases build one call at a time. DBI/duckdb remain optional (Suggests).
  • txs_list_years(), txs_list_downloads(), txs_cite(), and the cache tooling all understand source = "peims". No FERPA masking applies to this source (amounts, not student counts).

Data dictionary and duckplyr (2026-07)

  • New machine-readable data dictionary at inst/data-dict.yaml (https://data-dict.tidyverse.org format, spec 0.1.0): documents every table the package returns – the TAPR semantic shapes, statewide TAPR/AEIS files, the TAPR variable dictionary, SRC, the directory, and PEIMS finance (plus its DuckDB provenance table) – with column types, ranges, masking semantics, cross-table relationships, and a glossary of TEA terms. Access it with system.file("data-dict.yaml", package = "txschools").
  • README’s DuckDB section now also covers duckplyr as the no-database way to run dplyr pipelines on DuckDB’s engine.

PEIMS money-flow diagrams (2026-07)

  • New txs_peims_flow(): aggregates a txs_get_peims_finance() pull into an income-statement-style flow edge list across chosen axes (revenue source, fund, function, object class, program intent). Every edge is a genuine recorded total – sources trace to spending through funds, the one join TEA’s accounting actually records – and each fund’s shortfall/surplus reconciles against explicit from/to fund-balance nodes.
  • New txs_plot_peims_flow(): renders the edge list as a Sankey diagram via the ggsankey package (GitHub-only; in Suggests with a guarded, informative error when absent). Returns a normal ggplot.
  • New vignette money-flow-diagrams: the concepts behind honest money-flow charts (recorded joins vs allocation, funds as the traceable link, fund-balance reconciliation) and the same charts built with ggsankey, ggalluvial, plotly, and networkD3.

Tax rates, geography, and the district viewer (2026-07)

  • The txschoolviewer project is absorbed into txschools, including its uncommitted app improvements. Its targets pipeline is replaced by package getters + txs_viewer_prepare(); targets is not a dependency.
  • New source txs_get_tax_rates(): district M&O/I&S property-tax rates, 2005-06 onward – Texas Comptroller rates-and-levies workbooks (primary, tax years 2019+) backfilled by TEA’s adopted-tax-rates workbook, with per-row provenance. MCR is a pluggable mcr argument pending an official statewide source; txs_derive_pennies() adds the HB3 Tier One/golden/copper decomposition and txs_homestead_exemption() the exemption schedule.
  • New geography helpers: txs_crosswalk() (TEA district number to NCES LEAID/Census GEOID, via the Urban Institute Education Data API) and txs_boundaries() (simplified Census district boundaries via tigris/sf).
  • New txs_viewer(): the interactive district tax-rate map explorer (MapLibre via mapgl; animated choropleth, district search, taxes-on-a-home mode, comparison tab), shipped in inst/viewer/ with all app dependencies in Suggests. txs_viewer_prepare() bakes its data from the package getters into the cache.
  • Follow-ups recorded, not implemented: wiring an official MCR source; a shinylive build of the viewer (geojson boundaries, no runtime sf); a viewer screenshot/vignette.

TAPR attendance fix (2026-07)

  • TEA’s standalone TAPR attendance endpoint has never produced output; the attendance semantic dataset silently returned zero rows. It is now served as the attendance/absenteeism slice of TEA’s combined attendance-graduation-dropout page (the graduation page), which is where TEA publishes those measures.

  • The semantic page fetcher now detects SAS-broker error pages, refuses to cache them, warns like any other failed page, and treats previously cached error pages as stale (refetched automatically).

  • New vignette data-dictionaries: human-readable documentation of every table the package returns, rendered directly from the shipped data-dict.yaml so the vignette and the machine-readable dictionary cannot drift apart.

Finance tab for the district viewer (2026-07)

  • New third tab in txs_viewer(): an interactive PEIMS money-flow (Sankey) diagram for any district or charter, with school-year, budget-vs-actual, axis-preset, and category-lumping controls. Uses the same txs_peims_flow()/txs_plot_peims_flow() as the README and vignette examples, so the look is consistent everywhere.
  • New txs_viewer_prepare_finance(): a separate, optional bake step (default: last 5 school years, both budget and actual, both districts and charters) that fetches and aggregates PEIMS data away from campus-level (fin_unit) detail into a small district-wide summary, so the tab filters and redraws instantly with no live network calls. Slower than txs_viewer_prepare() (roughly 10-20 minutes by default) and entirely optional – the Map and Compare tabs work without it, and the Finance tab shows a plain instructional message rather than an error when it hasn’t been run.
  • The Finance tab’s chart engine (ggsankey, GitHub-only) stays a soft dependency checked only where the tab renders – it does not widen txs_viewer()’s hard package-guard list, so installing the viewer for the Map/Compare tabs never requires a non-CRAN package.
  • Bug fix in txs_peims_flow(): the fund-balance/transfer reconciliation could error (“arguments must have same length”) for any district-year with zero inter-fund transfers or zero other financing activity – a common case, not an edge case – because an internal label helper returned a stray length-1 value instead of character(0) on a zero-row input (a base::paste() recycling quirk). Fixed at the source; regression-tested.

txs_open_src() (2026-07)

  • New txs_open_src(geography, level, tab, browse): opens a campus or district’s Texas School Report Card at https://txschools.gov in a browser. Since 2020 that JavaScript site is the only place SRC reports live – txs_get_src() cannot scrape it (see its documented 2004-2019 coverage) – so this is the complement: browse = FALSE returns the URL without opening anything, useful for scripting.

Viewer polish (2026-07)

  • Finance tab’s school-year picker is a dropdown (selectInput) rather than a slider – the slider was carried over from the Map tab’s animated choropleth control without its reason to exist (the play-button animation), which a plain dropdown suits better for a five-choice, non-animated pick.
  • The Map tab’s district search and the Finance tab’s entity search now use server-side selectize (matching the existing Compare tab pattern) instead of embedding the full ~1,000-option list in the page HTML, clearing Shiny’s “large number of options” performance warning for both.

Strict request spacing (2026-10)

  • HTTP requests are now spaced strictly at the configured rate (options(txschools.rate_per_sec), default one per second), as the README promises. Previously httr2’s token bucket let up to 60 requests per host through in a burst before throttling began. The package now requires httr2 >= 1.1.1 (which txs_crosswalk() already needed).

FIRST financial integrity ratings (2026-10)

  • New source txs_get_first(): TEA’s Financial Integrity Rating System of Texas (FIRST) ratings for every district (School FIRST, 2002-03 onward) and charter (Charter FIRST, 2011-12 onward, including the separate university-charter list since 2017-18). One tidy row per district or charter and rating year: status, rating, letter grade (2015-16 onward), score, a fiscal_year key that lines each rating up with the PEIMS actuals it was computed from, and a release column. years are ending rating years (2026 means the 2025-26 ratings) and are required.
  • release flags preliminary ratings. Charter FIRST labels its workbooks correctly, but School FIRST titles every workbook “Final” – including the preliminary 2025-26 ratings – so district rows downloaded before December 1 of the rating year count as preliminary. Cached preliminary copies are never replaced silently; the function points to refresh = TRUE once finals are due.
  • TEA serves FIRST only through two ASP.NET search apps (no files, no API), so each workbook is fetched in a short cookie session: page, year postback, Download (plus a list postback for university charters). The internal HTTP layer gains cookie-jar support and an in-memory form POST, and each workbook is checked (zip signature, header, title year, and list) before it is cached, so a silently failed postback can never cache the wrong year.
